reviews.comment: I do not fully recommend Gabrielle Lyle for any course. She is new to teaching, however, the way she presents her lectures sound like a 12 year old on an older model laptop. She also takes off way too many points just for one small mistake. I'll admit I am not a straight A student, but she can be way more lenient on her grading.

Very hard to hear as she pants for a breath between every syllable, and very quiet. And it's a History class (1302) without a textbook. Took me a while to figure out this was the same person, she's at SHSU now. It's presented to us like I would present to high school students. Got upset that people didn't want to watch (listen to) lectures.

I wanted to like this prof, I really did. She seems like a sweet person, but her teaching skills are poor. Mumbles during odd lectures, disorganized. Kind of felt like she was just dropped into this class with no training. Didn't feel like I learned anything more than what I already knew from high school. Do not recommend taking her.

Do not recommend this prof. I've never had a prof grade more strict than her. So be careful and make sure you cover all your bases before you submit or she will take off points. Attendance isn't mandatory but she does random exit tickets that count towards your grade. She will ask you to cite often too on many assignments. Not a lot of homework.

Disorganized, didn't cover enough topics. Spent too much time on niche subjects instead of learning what actually happened. Some students obv like this style with no exams, but it was a joke to me. This was her first class and it showed. Don't appreciate being the guinea pig for professors trying to figure out how to teach. Would not take again.

Fall 2023 was her first semester as a teacher, and it was quite apparent, as in the first half her essays had really low word counts and her grading was tough. However, as time passed, she became more understanding and caring towards students, and grading has become much more reasonable. Great teacher, LOTS OF WRITING.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are no exams or quizzes whatsoever. Most of your grade is essays. There are 8, 500 word essays based on a piece of media (book, documentary, movie) and lecture. Each has a writing guide, so as long as you follow that your grade will be fine. She's super sweet and gives feedback on all of your essays.

The course consisted of 3 books, 8 500 word journal reflections, 6 group assigmemts, and around 10 spontaneous exit tickets essentially counting towards attendance. It seems like a lot of work, but considering the college workload and difficulty this was essentially a high school class. Very nice and prof, with no exams or quizzes!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ms. Lyle was by far one of the best history profs i'd ever had. Lots of writings, but she puts out a template  for you to follow, which makes it pretty easy. She is a bit quirky, but she's really sweet and her lectures were actually interesting. She does do exit tickets, but they're spread out throughout the semester. Overall would recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't listen to these other ones! Ms Lyle is AMAZING, no exams, short biweekly essays that are so simple if you follow the criteria. She is so kind and strives to make sure everyone understands what she expects.  She is a bit quirky, but so endearing...and we are all quirky.  You can afford to miss a few classes if you are strategic. Loved her!!
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this as a 5 week summer class and I found it an easy A. You have to go to class bc she does exit tickets and group projects. Weekly 150 word assignments about books and a final long essay about some cartoon book. No exams!!! She is boring and mumbles though.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Odd class, odd teacher. Difficult to hear and understand, confusing assignments, tough grader. Doesn't seem like she knows what she's talking about sometimes. Nice lady, very friendly. Kind of feels like maybe she shouldn't be teaching. Kind of out of her league? Recommend taking someone else, especially if you want to actually learn something.
